svg.text: Visual conventions: MySQL Workbench 26.7 · Data and analysis: myflames
Data flows downward. Colors identify operators; arrow width represents estimated rows on a log scale.
Join circles show the reported join type: left joins include the whole left circle; inner joins highlight the overlap.
Select a node for details. Drag to pan, scroll gently to zoom, or use Fit plan and the zoom buttons.
materialization=on — A subquery or derived table is executed once and its result stored in a temporary table for reuse. It may spill to disk past tmp_table_size (MySQL's
TempTable engine) or the smaller of tmp_table_size and max_heap_table_size (MEMORY engine, MariaDB).
1 temp table(s) (Materialize) — up to 5 rows; may spill to disk
1 sort operation(s) — 5 rows; may use disk-based filesort
• Check internal_tmp_mem_storage_engine and temporary-table disk usage before raising tmp_table_size. Why: the default TempTable engine limits each in-memory internal temporary
table by tmp_table_size, and max_heap_table_size does not apply to it; only the MEMORY engine also uses max_heap_table_size, taking the smaller of the two. A temporary table in
the plan does not by itself show that it spilled to disk.
• Increase sort_buffer_size or add an ordered index to avoid filesort
⚠ Filesort detected with sort_buffer_size=256.0 KB. Whether it spills depends on the sort's row count and record size.
⚠ Query materializes 1 temp table(s); tmp_table_size is 16.0 MB. This limit alone does not show whether a table spilled to disk.
• Check sort merge passes and query timing before increasing sort_buffer_size for this session. Why: when sort records exceed the buffer, MySQL can write sorted runs and merge
them. A larger buffer may avoid that work; small sorts may already fit in memory. Test session-level changes and account for concurrent sorting sessions before changing the
• Check the internal temporary-table engine and disk usage before increasing tmp_table_size for this session. Why: MySQL 8.0.28+ TempTable uses tmp_table_size as its per-table
limit; max_heap_table_size does not limit TempTable. Shared TempTable RAM and mmap limits also affect disk usage. If the internal engine is MEMORY, the smaller of tmp_table_size
